key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage in perovskite solar cells, identifying preferential degradation at the buried hole-transport-layer interface.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive optical screening can guide buried-interface design, with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification improving UV stability in perovskite films and devices.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe different depths with photoluminescence excitation.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL, and ideality-factor measurements during UV-soaking studies.
Compare films and p-i-n solar cells with different indium tin oxide interface modifiers.
evidence_signal: Non-destructive measurements localized UV degradation to the buried interface, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests, and showed reduced damage after interface modification.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative stability gains, and UV-soaking results alone do not establish durability under broader operating conditions.
paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
